metadata.title: Assessment evidence guide for enterprise IT

remarks.p: Consumers of this file should refer to the Essentials OSCAL NS 1.0 page for information regarding the Essentials specific representation used in this OSCAL file.

part.name: overview
part.p: The board of directors or executive committee is accountable for cyber security.

part.name: statement
part.p: Formally define and establish executive and board-level accountabilities for cyber security, including setting, monitoring and adjusting organisational risk appetite, and review these accountabilities at a defined cadence.

part.name: item
part.p: No named executive or board member is accountable for cyber security.

part.name: item
part.p: Cyber security accountability exists only informally, or is assumed rather than documented.

part.name: item
part.p: No evidence of cyber security reporting to the executive board.

part.name: item
part.p: Organisational risk appetite is not set.

part.name: item
part.p: A named executive or board member is accountable for cyber security, but reporting obligations are not formally defined.

part.name: item
part.p: Board-level reporting on cyber security occurs but is ad hoc rather than on a defined schedule.

part.name: item
part.p: Accountability is documented but has not been reviewed within the organisationally defined cadence or following relevant organisational restructuring or leadership changes.

part.name: item
part.p: Organisational risk appetite is set but is not monitored or adjusted over time.

part.name: item
part.p: A named executive or board member has documented accountability for cyber security with defined reporting obligations.

part.name: item
part.p: Regular reporting to the board or executives occurs on a defined cadence with evidence of reporting artefacts.

part.name: item
part.p: Accountability arrangements are reviewed when organisational structures or leadership changes occur.

part.name: item
part.p: Organisational risk appetite is set and is monitored and adjusted over time as required.

part.name: overview
part.p: The board of directors or executive committee is accountable for ensuring that artificial intelligence is secure, controllable, human-supervised and used in an ethical and accountable manner.

part.name: statement
part.p: Establish and maintain executive accountability for the use, governance and risk management of artificial intelligence within the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: No named executive is accountable for the use, governance or risk management of artificial intelligence.

part.name: item
part.p: Artificial intelligence is used within the organisation with no approval, risk assessment or oversight.

part.name: item
part.p: Artificial intelligence related risks are not reflected in the organisation’s risk register.

part.name: item
part.p: Artificial intelligence use and governance arrangements have not been reviewed within the schedule defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: A named executive is accountable for artificial intelligence but the governance process is informal or undocumented.

part.name: item
part.p: Approval and risk assessment occur for some artificial intelligence use cases but coverage is inconsistent across internally developed, third-party and embedded artificial intelligence.

part.name: item
part.p: Some artificial intelligence related risks are recorded but the organisation’s risk register does not capture all known artificial intelligence use cases.

part.name: item
part.p: Reviews occur within the schedule defined by the organisation, but do not consistently address changes in artificial intelligence capability, threat environment or organisational use.

part.name: item
part.p: A named executive has accountability for artificial intelligence, supported by an approved governance process that has evidence of being followed.

part.name: item
part.p: The governance process addresses approval, risk assessment and oversight for internally developed, third-party and embedded artificial intelligence use cases.

part.name: item
part.p: Artificial intelligence related risks are reflected in the organisation’s risk register and reported through standard governance channels.

part.name: item
part.p: Reviews of artificial intelligence use and governance arrangements are conducted on a schedule defined by the organisation and consistently address changes in artificial intelligence capability, threat environment or organisational use.

part.name: overview
part.p: Suitable and sufficient personnel and resources are identified, acquired and maintained in support of cyber security activities.

part.name: statement
part.p: Assign sufficient cyber security personnel and resources with the required skills to operate, monitor, maintain and manage the lifecycle of security controls and define cyber security responsibilities within role descriptions.

part.name: item
part.p: Cyber security functions are staffed on an ad hoc basis without reference to required skills or capacity.

part.name: item
part.p: Critical cyber security roles are unfilled with no approved recruitment plan.

part.name: item
part.p: No resourcing plan for cyber security personnel exists.

part.name: item
part.p: Some critical roles are filled but identified skills gaps have no plan for remediation.

part.name: item
part.p: While assigned personnel provide some capability, there are gaps in capacity, resources, or expertise that hinder the operation, monitoring, maintenance, and lifecycle management of controls.

part.name: item
part.p: A resourcing plan exists but does not cover all required cyber security functions.

part.name: item
part.p: Outstanding cyber security positions are being actively recruited, but capacity or skills gaps remain.

part.name: item
part.p: Sufficient cyber security personnel are assigned to operate, monitor, maintain and manage the lifecycle of controls across the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Skills gaps are identified and addressed through recruitment, training or contracted services.

part.name: item
part.p: A resourcing plan identifies all required cyber security personnel, roles, skills, resources and capacity.

part.name: item
part.p: Cyber security responsibilities are defined within applicable role descriptions.

part.name: statement
part.p: Periodically review cyber security resourcing against cyber threat trends, cyber security incident outcomes and organisational changes.

part.name: item
part.p: No review of cyber security resourcing has been conducted.

part.name: item
part.p: Resourcing has not been reassessed following significant organisational or threat landscape changes.

part.name: item
part.p: A review has been conducted but did not reference current threat trends, cyber security incident outcomes, or organisational changes.

part.name: item
part.p: Review outcomes have identified required adjustments, but those adjustments have not been made.

part.name: item
part.p: A resourcing review has been completed within the review period defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: The review references current threat trends, cyber security incident outcomes and organisational changes.

part.name: item
part.p: Documented review outcomes include resourcing adjustments that are implemented within timeframes defined by the organisation, or formally risk accepted by an appropriate authority.

part.name: overview
part.p: Security risk management activities for an organisation and their systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are embedded into organisational risk management frameworks and subject to ongoing monitoring and assurance activities by the board of directors or executive committee.

part.name: statement
part.p: Establish and maintain an approved risk management methodology and plan that is used to assess and treat cyber security risks.

part.name: item
part.p: No risk management methodology approved by the organisation is in place.

part.name: item
part.p: No current organisational risk register exists, or the register has not been reviewed within the cycle defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Risk treatment decisions are not documented.

part.name: item
part.p: An approved risk management methodology exists but risk assessments have not been conducted within the defined cycle.

part.name: item
part.p: A risk register exists but treatment plans are incomplete or have not been actioned.

part.name: item
part.p: Risk assessments have been conducted but do not cover all in-scope assets.

part.name: item
part.p: An approved risk management methodology and plan are in place and used to assess and treat security risks.

part.name: item
part.p: A current risk register exists with documented and implemented treatment plans for all identified risks.

part.name: item
part.p: Risk assessments have been conducted or reviewed within the assessment cycle defined by the organisation.

part.name: overview
part.p: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are delivered and supported by trustworthy suppliers whose cyber security practices are regularly verified or otherwise risk-assessed.

part.name: statement
part.p: Select and engage suppliers of software, hardware and services on the basis of a cyber supply chain risk assessment proportionate to the risk the supplier introduces, and retain appropriate assurance evidence to support the decision.

part.name: item
part.p: No documented or approved governance process exists for evaluating the cyber security trustworthiness of suppliers.

part.name: item
part.p: No cyber security evaluation is performed before suppliers are onboarded.

part.name: item
part.p: Evaluation outcomes are not documented.

part.name: item
part.p: Findings from supplier evaluation outcomes are not used to inform supplier approval, contractual requirements or risk treatment decisions where concerns are identified.

part.name: item
part.p: An evaluation process exists but is not consistently applied to all suppliers within scope.

part.name: item
part.p: Evaluation is performed for some suppliers, but criteria are not documented or are inconsistently applied.

part.name: item
part.p: Outcomes are documented but contractual arrangements do not reflect identified risks or required controls.

part.name: item
part.p: A documented and approved governance process is in place and consistently applied.

part.name: item
part.p: Cyber security trustworthiness evaluations are performed for all suppliers within scope prior to onboarding.

part.name: item
part.p: Evaluation criteria are documented, approved and proportionate to the criticality of what the supplier delivers.

part.name: item
part.p: Evaluation outcomes are documented, reflected in contractual arrangements and recorded in the organisation’s risk register where residual risk remains.

part.name: statement
part.p: Maintain current assurance that suppliers continue to meet their cyber security commitments, and act when that assurance lapses or the supplier’s risk changes.

part.name: item
part.p: No process exists to obtain and risk-assess current supplier assurance evidence proportionate to supplier criticality and risk.

part.name: item
part.p: No documented and approved governance process exists for maintaining assurance that suppliers meet their cyber security commitments.

part.name: item
part.p: No actions are taken when supplier cyber security assurance lapses or supplier risk changes.

part.name: item
part.p: Supplier assurance evidence is obtained for some suppliers, but coverage is incomplete or the evidence is not reviewed and actioned.

part.name: item
part.p: Some findings are actioned but the response process is informal or inconsistent.

part.name: item
part.p: A process exists but acceptable forms and currency of assurance evidence are not defined or applied consistently.

part.name: item
part.p: Current assurance evidence is obtained from suppliers in proportion to their criticality and risk, and is reviewed for findings that affect the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Material concerns are addressed through contractual remediation, compensating controls or supplier substitution within defined timeframes.

part.name: item
part.p: A documented and approved governance process specifies the acceptable forms, scope and currency of supplier assurance evidence.

part.name: overview
part.p: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) that are not capable of meeting cyber security requirements are managed using compensating security controls, along with enhanced monitoring and assurance activities, to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until they can be decommissioned or replaced.

part.name: statement
part.p: Establish and maintain a process for identifying, assessing and treating cyber security risks associated with legacy systems and unsupported technologies through compensating controls, enhanced monitoring and assurance until the systems can be removed or replaced.

part.name: item
part.p: No documented or approved governance process exists for identifying or managing legacy systems.

part.name: item
part.p: Legacy systems are not formally identified within the environment.

part.name: item
part.p: Cyber security risks associated with legacy systems are not assessed or are assessed informally.

part.name: item
part.p: There are no interim compensating controls to manage identified cyber security risks associated with legacy systems.

part.name: item
part.p: Legacy systems remain in operation indefinitely with no documented decommissioning, replacement or migration path.

part.name: item
part.p: A process exists but the criteria for classifying a system as legacy are not documented or are inconsistently applied.

part.name: item
part.p: Some legacy systems are identified but the inventory is incomplete or is not maintained.

part.name: item
part.p: Risk assessments are conducted for some legacy systems but treatment decisions are not documented or approved.

part.name: item
part.p: Some compensating controls are in place to address risks associated with legacy systems, but coverage is not complete.

part.name: item
part.p: A path exists for some legacy systems but is not tracked to completion.

part.name: item
part.p: A documented and approved governance process exists with clear criteria for classifying systems as legacy.

part.name: item
part.p: Legacy systems are formally identified, inventoried and reviewed on a cycle defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Cyber security risks associated with legacy systems are assessed, treated and approved by an appropriate authority.

part.name: item
part.p: Compensating controls are applied to manage cyber security risks for legacy systems while decommissioning or migration efforts are in progress.

part.name: item
part.p: A documented decommissioning, replacement or migration path exists for retained legacy systems and is tracked to completion.

part.name: overview
part.p: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications, identities, credentials and data) are continually and centrally identified and documented.

part.name: statement
part.p: Use an approved asset inventory mechanism that supports automated discovery to detect new and changed physical and non-physical assets.

part.name: item
part.p: No approved asset inventory mechanism is in place.

part.name: item
part.p: Asset inventory records are maintained manually with no automated discovery capability.

part.name: item
part.p: An approved asset inventory mechanism is deployed but does not cover all network segments or asset types.

part.name: item
part.p: Automated discovery scans to detect new and changed physical and non-physical assets occur on a schedule but reconciliation with the approved inventory is manual or inconsistent.

part.name: item
part.p: An approved asset inventory mechanism which supports automated discovery is deployed to cover all applicable assets and network segments.

part.name: item
part.p: Discovery runs on a regular schedule defined by the organisation and new or changed physical or non-physical assets that are detected are reconciled with the approved inventory.

part.name: statement
part.p: Maintain current records of infrastructure, operating systems, applications, identities, credentials and data assets.

part.name: item
part.p: A maintained record of infrastructure, operating systems, applications, identities, credentials and data assets has not been established.

part.name: item
part.p: There is no defined process for identifying, recording, reviewing and updating asset records.

part.name: item
part.p: Asset records are maintained, but identified omissions, inaccuracies or newly discovered assets are not triaged and addressed within the timeframes or tolerances defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: A process to update the asset inventory runs on a schedule but the results are not reconciled or updated within a period defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: At each scheduled review or update, records of infrastructure, operating systems, applications, identities, credentials and data assets are complete and accurate within the tolerances defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: A defined process identifies changes and newly discovered assets between scheduled reviews, and ensures that records are reviewed, reconciled and updated within timeframes commensurate with the associated cyber security risk.

part.name: overview
part.p: Security risks for an organisation and their systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are identified, including by using current strategic and sector-specific cyber threat intelligence and threat modelling, and are documented along with any associated risk management decisions.

part.name: statement
part.p: Identify relevant weaknesses, malicious actor techniques and cyber threat behaviours when undertaking risk assessments and review these inputs on a continuous basis.

part.name: item
part.p: Risk assessments do not reference relevant weaknesses, malicious actor techniques and cyber threat behaviours.

part.name: item
part.p: No process exists to incorporate threat information into risk assessment activities.

part.name: item
part.p: Current weaknesses, malicious actor techniques and cyber threat behaviours that are relevant to the organisation are not reviewed or updated.

part.name: item
part.p: Risk assessments reference threat intelligence but coverage is limited to well-known or generic threats.

part.name: item
part.p: Threat information is considered but not systematically mapped to organisational assets or detection gaps.

part.name: item
part.p: Current weaknesses, malicious actor techniques and cyber threat behaviours that are relevant to the organisation are reviewed or updated, but are not used to inform risk assessments or are reviewed only on an ad hoc basis.

part.name: item
part.p: Risk assessments incorporate and reference relevant weaknesses, malicious actor techniques relevant to the sector, and cyber threat behaviours.

part.name: item
part.p: Relevant weaknesses, malicious actor techniques and cyber threat behaviours are systematically related to applicable assets and used to inform risk treatment decisions.

part.name: item
part.p: Current weaknesses, malicious actor techniques and cyber threat behaviours relevant to the organisation are reviewed or updated on a continuous basis at a frequency that enables noted changes to inform risk assessments.

part.name: overview
part.p: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems and applications) are planned, designed, developed, tested, deployed, maintained and decommissioned according to their business criticality ratings and security and resilience requirements using Secure by Design and Secure by Default principles and practices.

link.text: Mitigated technique: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation

part.name: statement
part.p: Design systems securely to provide visibility, enforce authorised access, protect data, minimise required and default privileges, limit exposed services and remove unnecessary functionality.

part.name: item
part.p: Systems are deployed with default configurations and no evidence of security design considerations.

part.name: item
part.p: Unnecessary services, protocols or functionality remain enabled with no documented rationale.

part.name: item
part.p: Security telemetry is not enabled or is not considered as part of system design.

part.name: item
part.p: Security is considered during system design but not consistently applied across all assets.

part.name: item
part.p: Some unnecessary services have been disabled but a systematic review has not been completed.

part.name: item
part.p: Security telemetry is partially enabled but gaps in coverage exist.

part.name: item
part.p: Systems are designed and deployed with exposed services limited, required and default permissions minimised, data protections in place, authorised access enforced, and only required functionality enabled.

part.name: item
part.p: Security telemetry is enabled by default.

part.name: item
part.p: Evidence exists that security design decisions are recorded and reviewed during system changes.

part.name: statement
part.p: Secure build and deployment processes to enforce controls consistently across systems.

part.name: item
part.p: No controlled build or deployment process exists for applicable assets.

part.name: item
part.p: Changes to systems are applied ad hoc, without any version control, testing or approval.

part.name: item
part.p: A controlled deployment process exists but is not consistently followed for all changes.

part.name: item
part.p: Version control is in place but pre-deployment security verification is not performed.

part.name: item
part.p: A controlled build and deployment process is in place and consistently followed.

part.name: item
part.p: Configuration changes are subject to version control, testing and approval before deployment.

part.name: item
part.p: Security controls are confirmed to be implemented consistently across systems following deployment processes.

part.name: overview
part.p: Cyber supply chains supporting systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are secure, resilient and support effective and coordinated cyber security incident response.

part.name: statement
part.p: Assess the integrity and authenticity of software, components and updates before use, and verify provenance where suitable supplier evidence is available.

part.name: item
part.p: No verification of software, component or update integrity or authenticity is performed before introduction into systems.

part.name: item
part.p: Verification outcomes are not recorded or available for review.

part.name: item
part.p: Where verification cannot be performed, no compensating control or remediation paths are documented.

part.name: item
part.p: Verification is performed for some categories of software but not consistently across operating systems, applications, firmware and dependencies.

part.name: item
part.p: Integrity or provenance checks are performed, but they do not provide sufficient assurance for all software, components or updates.

part.name: item
part.p: Verification outcomes are recorded for some software, components or updates prior to being introduced into systems, but not consistently.

part.name: item
part.p: Compensating controls exist for some unverifiable components but are not formally approved or time-bound.

part.name: item
part.p: Verification of integrity and provenance is performed for software, components and updates across all relevant categories, and provenance is verified where suitable supplier evidence is available.

part.name: item
part.p: Verification uses one or more mechanisms appropriate to the software, component, update and source to provide reliable assurance of integrity and provenance.

part.name: item
part.p: Verification outcomes are recorded and available for review.

part.name: item
part.p: Where verification cannot be performed, compensating controls are applied, exceptions are time-bound and remediation paths are documented.

part.name: statement
part.p: Use vendor advisories and threat intelligence to maintain awareness of supplier, product and component exposure to compromise, and act within timeframes proportionate to the risk.

part.name: item
part.p: No monitoring is performed for indicators of supply chain compromise affecting software, components or services in use.

part.name: item
part.p: Vendor security notifications and threat advisories are not reviewed or actioned.

part.name: item
part.p: When supply chain compromise is identified, neither containment nor investigation is performed.

part.name: item
part.p: Supply chain compromise events are integrated into neither incident response nor risk management.

part.name: item
part.p: Monitoring occurs but does not draw on relevant threat intelligence sources or does not cover all in-scope systems.

part.name: item
part.p: Notifications and advisories are reviewed but exposure assessment and response are not conducted in a timely manner.

part.name: item
part.p: Containment occurs but investigation for evidence of exploitation is not consistently undertaken.

part.name: item
part.p: Some integration exists but findings are not reflected in the risk register or incident response procedures.

part.name: item
part.p: Monitoring covers software, components and services in use, drawing on relevant threat intelligence sources.

part.name: item
part.p: Vendor security notifications and threat advisories are reviewed, exposure is assessed and response actions are initiated within defined timeframes.

part.name: item
part.p: Identified supply chain compromises are responded to in timeframes defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Supply chain compromise events are integrated with incident response and reflected in the risk register.

group.title: PRO-13 - Identity, credential and access management

part.name: overview
part.p: Robust and secure identity, credential and access management is used to establish, maintain and control access to systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) and to support effective detection of identity and credential misuse.

part.name: statement
part.p: Identify and disable or remove default and unused accounts regularly, permitting exceptions only where the account is documented, justified, hardened and monitored.

part.name: item
part.p: No review of default or unused accounts has been conducted within the review period defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Default vendor accounts remain enabled on production systems without appropriate documentation, justification, hardening and monitoring in place for their use.

part.name: item
part.p: No process exists to identify accounts that have not authenticated within a defined period.

part.name: item
part.p: A review has been conducted but does not cover all assets.

part.name: item
part.p: Default accounts have been identified but some remain enabled without documented justification.

part.name: item
part.p: Unused accounts are identified but remediation is incomplete or delayed beyond defined timeframes.

part.name: item
part.p: A review of accounts has been completed within the defined review period covering all assets.

part.name: item
part.p: Default accounts are disabled or have approved justification for remaining active, with appropriate monitoring and compensating controls for their use in place.

part.name: item
part.p: Accounts that show no evidence of use, other than approved emergency access accounts, are identified and either disabled or removed in accordance with defined timeframes.

link.text: Mitigated technique: Credentials from Password Stores

part.name: statement
part.p: Store authentication keys, secrets and tokens in approved secure repositories with access controls, including MFA.

part.name: item
part.p: Credentials are stored in plaintext, spreadsheets, shared drives or other unapproved locations as standard practice.

part.name: item
part.p: No approved secure repository is in use to store authentication keys, secrets and tokens.

part.name: item
part.p: Access to credential stores is neither controlled nor audited.

part.name: item
part.p: Access controls such as MFA are not enabled for authentication to secure repositories.

part.name: item
part.p: An approved secure repository is in use but does not cover all authentication keys, secrets and tokens within scope.

part.name: item
part.p: Access controls for secure repositories are in place but access logging is not enabled or not reviewed.

part.name: item
part.p: MFA is enforced for some, but not all, applicable users, repositories or authentication pathways, and the remaining exceptions are documented and subject to remediation.

part.name: item
part.p: Authentication keys, secrets and tokens within scope are stored in approved secure repositories, with any authorised exceptions documented, risk-assessed and managed in accordance with organisationally defined requirements.

part.name: item
part.p: Access to secure repositories is restricted using attribute or role-based access controls, MFA is enforced for all applicable authentication pathways, and access is logged and reviewed and investigated where necessary.

part.name: statement
part.p: Identify and remediate unsecured keys, secrets and credentials by regularly scanning codebases, configuration files, file shares and user collaboration platforms.

part.name: item
part.p: No secret scanning capability is deployed.

part.name: item
part.p: No process exists to identify credentials exposed in codebases, configuration files, file shares or user collaboration platforms.

part.name: item
part.p: Unsecured keys, secrets and credentials found exposed in codebases, configuration files, scripts, file shares or user collaboration platforms are left in place with no action taken.

part.name: item
part.p: Secret scanning is deployed but does not cover all repositories, pipelines or user collaboration platforms.

part.name: item
part.p: Scanning runs but discovered credentials are not assessed in a timely manner.

part.name: item
part.p: Unsecured keys, secrets and credentials that are discovered are assessed, but are not rotated or revoked in a timely manner.

part.name: item
part.p: Secret scanning tooling is deployed across codebases, configuration files, file shares and user collaboration platforms.

part.name: item
part.p: Scans to identify unsecured keys, secrets and credentials run on a regular schedule defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Unsecured keys, secrets and credentials that are discovered are assessed, then rotated and/or revoked within timeframes defined by the organisation.

link.text: Mitigated technique: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation

part.name: statement
part.p: Use phishing-resistant MFA for users authenticating to systems, including from untrusted, external or high-risk locations.

part.name: item
part.p: Phishing-resistant MFA is not enforced for interactive user authentication to systems.

part.name: item
part.p: MFA is deployed but uses non-phishing-resistant methods, such as SMS, voice, or push-only authentication instead of phishing-resistant MFA.

part.name: item
part.p: No access policies differentiate between trusted and untrusted, external or high-risk locations.

part.name: item
part.p: Access from untrusted, external or high-risk locations is permitted without MFA, or with non-phishing-resistant MFA.

part.name: item
part.p: Phishing-resistant MFA is deployed for some but not all systems within scope.

part.name: item
part.p: Access policies exist but do not cover all organisationally defined high-risk location categories.

part.name: item
part.p: Exceptions or alternative authentication pathways allow routine or recurring authentication without phishing-resistant MFA, or emergency access arrangements are not adequately restricted, monitored, tested or reviewed.

part.name: item
part.p: Phishing-resistant MFA is enforced for all routine interactive user authentication to systems within scope.

part.name: item
part.p: Phishing-resistant MFA is enforced for routine authentication attempts from untrusted, external or high-risk locations.

part.name: item
part.p: Customer-facing services provide a phishing-resistant MFA option for authentication.

part.name: item
part.p: Emergency access arrangements are periodically tested and reviewed to confirm that they remain operational, appropriately protected and limited to their intended purpose. Credentials or authentication factors used for emergency access are securely managed and are not used for routine administration.

part.name: statement
part.p: Disable legacy authentication protocols or, where this is not feasible, restrict and monitor their use, apply compensating controls and establish a time-bound decommissioning plan.

part.name: item
part.p: Legacy authentication protocols that cannot enforce modern authentication controls remain enabled and in active use without restriction.

part.name: item
part.p: No assessment has been conducted to identify which legacy authentication protocols are in use within the environment.

part.name: item
part.p: Authentication mechanisms transmitting credentials in cleartext or using weak cryptographic primitives remain enabled and no action has been taken to disable them.

part.name: item
part.p: Where legacy protocols are retained, no compensating controls, no monitoring and no decommissioning timelines are in place.

part.name: item
part.p: Legacy authentication protocols have been identified and are partially restricted but some remain enabled across systems within scope without justification.

part.name: item
part.p: An assessment has been conducted but does not cover all in-scope systems, or the inventory of legacy protocols in use is not maintained.

part.name: item
part.p: Some weak authentication mechanisms have been disabled but others remain enabled without documented justification or remediation plan.

part.name: item
part.p: Compensating controls exist for some retained legacy protocols but monitoring is inconsistent or decommissioning timelines are not defined.

part.name: item
part.p: Legacy authentication protocols that cannot enforce modern authentication controls have been identified and disabled across systems within scope, excluding documented and risk accepted exceptions.

part.name: item
part.p: An assessment of legacy authentication protocol use has been conducted across in-scope systems and the inventory is maintained.

part.name: item
part.p: Where retention is necessary, compensating controls are applied and decommissioning timelines are recorded and tracked.

part.name: item
part.p: Ongoing use of legacy authentication protocols is regularly risk reviewed, accepted and recorded in the organisation’s risk register.

part.name: statement
part.p: Ensure that user, machine, system and service account credentials are unique per system or account, particularly in high-privilege contexts.

part.name: item
part.p: Local administrator credentials are shared across the device fleet, or service or privileged account credentials are routinely reused across systems.

part.name: item
part.p: Credential uniqueness is not enforced for applicable user, machine, system or service identities.

part.name: item
part.p: Credential uniqueness has not been addressed in high-privilege contexts, including domain administration, cloud administration or automation platforms.

part.name: item
part.p: Where credential uniqueness cannot be enforced, neither compensating controls nor remediation paths are in place.

part.name: item
part.p: Local administrator credential uniqueness has been implemented for some device populations but coverage is incomplete across the device fleet.

part.name: item
part.p: A technical mechanism is in place but applies to only a subset of credential types or systems within scope.

part.name: item
part.p: Credential uniqueness has been addressed in some high-privilege contexts but gaps remain in others.

part.name: item
part.p: Compensating controls exist for some shared credentials but monitoring is inconsistent or remediation plans do not exist.

part.name: item
part.p: Credentials for applicable local administrative accounts are unique to each system or account.

part.name: item

part.name: item
part.p: The cadence of review is not defined.

part.name: item
part.p: Training is reviewed but updates do not reflect current threat intelligence, sector relevant adversary techniques or organisational changes.

part.name: item
part.p: Some lessons are incorporated but the process is informal, or coverage is limited to a small number of incidents.

part.name: item
part.p: Some changes are reflected, but training is not updated to address recently introduced systems or significant changes to working arrangements.

part.name: item
part.p: A review cadence exists, but is not consistently met, or is not proportionate to the rate of change.

part.name: item
part.p: Training content is reviewed and updated on a defined cycle, with updates reflecting current threat intelligence, adversary techniques relevant to the workforce and organisation’s operating context.

part.name: item
part.p: Lessons learnt from cyber security incidents within the organisation or its sector are systematically incorporated into training content.

part.name: item
part.p: Training reflects the systems, platforms and working arrangements that personnel currently interact with, including newly introduced platforms and changes to ways of working.

part.name: item
part.p: The cadence of review is defined, proportionate to the rate of change in the threat environment, and consistently met.

part.name: overview
part.p: Security-relevant event logs and configuration changes for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are centrally collected, protected against unauthorised modification or deletion, and retained to support effective cyber security event detection and investigation.

link.text: Mitigated technique: Disable or Modify Tools

part.name: statement
part.p: Protect event logs from unauthorised access, modification or deletion, including by encrypting them during transit and at rest and securing the systems and accounts used to store, manage and analyse them.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs generated by applicable assets are not protected from modification or deletion.

part.name: item
part.p: Log access is not restricted to authorised roles with a business need.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are neither encrypted during transit nor at rest.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are forwarded but integrity protections are not in place at the source.

part.name: item
part.p: Log access is restricted but some roles retain the ability to modify or delete logs.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are encrypted during transit but are not protected with encryption at rest (or vice versa).

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are protected against modification or deletion.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are encrypted in transit and at rest.

part.name: item
part.p: Access to logs is restricted to authorised roles with a business need.

link.text: Mitigated technique: Disable or Modify Tools

part.name: statement
part.p: Forward high-value, security-relevant event logs and configuration changes from infrastructure, operating systems and applications to a central log storage capability.

part.name: item
part.p: Security-relevant logs from assets are not forwarded to a central logging capability.

part.name: item
part.p: High-value, security-relevant event logs or configuration changes from infrastructure, operating systems or applications are not forwarded.

part.name: item
part.p: High-value, security-relevant event logs are forwarded, but coverage gaps are identified or completeness has not been validated.

part.name: item
part.p: Configuration change logs are forwarded inconsistently.

part.name: item
part.p: The utility of security log sources is reviewed, but on an ad hoc basis rather than according to a defined schedule.

part.name: item
part.p: Log forwarding is in place but latency is excessive for effective detection.

part.name: item
part.p: High-value security-relevant event logs and configuration changes from all relevant infrastructure, operating systems and application sources are forwarded to the central logging capability.

part.name: item
part.p: Security log sources are reviewed at regular intervals to ensure their continued utility in detecting and responding to changing adversary techniques.

part.name: item
part.p: Log completeness has been validated against the expected log sources.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are forwarded at a frequency that enables timely detection.

link.text: Mitigated technique: Disable or Modify Tools

part.name: statement
part.p: Establish a centralised event log storage capability that protects logs from unauthorised access or modification.

part.name: item
part.p: No centralised capability exists for storing event logs collected from systems across the environment.

part.name: item
part.p: Stored logs have no protection against modification or deletion by administrators of the systems generating them.

part.name: item
part.p: Access to the centralised capability is not restricted, or access is granted to roles without a documented need.

part.name: item
part.p: Log retention requirements are not defined.

part.name: item
part.p: A centralised capability exists but does not receive logs from in-scope systems, or coverage is inconsistent.

part.name: item
part.p: Stored logs are protected from modification, but the controls do not consistently prevent deletion, or controls are not applied to all log types.

part.name: item
part.p: Access is restricted to a defined set of roles but access is not logged or monitored.

part.name: item
part.p: A retention period is defined but is inconsistently applied, or some log types are retained for shorter periods than required.

part.name: item
part.p: A centralised event log storage capability is in place for logs collected from in-scope systems.

part.name: item
part.p: Stored logs are protected against unauthorised access, modification and deletion through technical controls including access restrictions, encryption at rest and integrity protection.

part.name: item
part.p: Access to the centralised capability is restricted to security operations personnel and other roles with a documented need, with access logged and monitored.

part.name: item
part.p: Log retention requirements are defined and aligned to investigative, regulatory and contractual obligations, with retention applied consistently across log types.

part.name: overview
part.p: Baseline patterns of identity and credential access activities, privileged access activities, and remote access activities are established and maintained for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) to enable the detection of anomalous or unexpected behaviour.

link.text: Mitigated technique: System Binary Proxy Execution
Mitigated technique: Command and Scripting Interpreter

part.name: statement
part.p: Continuously monitor and analyse software execution behaviour on systems to detect where legitimate tools and utilities are being used for malicious purposes.

part.name: item
part.p: No monitoring or equivalent analysis is used to identify anomalous or unexpected use of legitimate tools and utilities on applicable systems.

part.name: item
part.p: Existing controls do not provide a reasonable capability to detect security-relevant patterns of legitimate software being used for malicious purposes.

part.name: item
part.p: Monitoring or equivalent analysis covers some priority tools, execution behaviours or applicable systems, but risk-significant coverage gaps exist.

part.name: item
part.p: Security-relevant execution telemetry is collected, but detection rules, behavioural analytics or equivalent analysis are incomplete or not consistently operational.

part.name: item
part.p: Alerts relating to anomalous or unexpected software execution are generated, but they are not consistently triaged and investigated within organisationally defined timeframes.

part.name: item
part.p: The organisation identifies the legitimate tools, utilities and execution behaviours that present heightened risk of malicious use within applicable systems.

part.name: item
part.p: Security-relevant telemetry and contextual information are analysed using detection rules, behavioural analytics or equivalent methods to identify anomalous or unexpected use of priority tools and utilities.

part.name: item
part.p: Detection coverage is periodically reviewed and adjusted in response to changes in applicable systems, threat intelligence, observed activity and the organisation’s risk profile.

part.name: item
part.p: Alerts are prioritised, triaged and investigated within timeframes defined according to their assessed security risk.

part.name: overview
part.p: Anomalous or unexpected events and behaviours for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are analysed in a timely manner to detect cyber security events.

part.name: statement
part.p: Ensure event logs are normalised, time-synchronised and enriched to support correlation across systems and environments.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are not time-synchronised to an authoritative source.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are ingested in raw format and are neither normalised nor enriched.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are time-synchronised but are not normalised to a common schema.

part.name: item
part.p: Some enrichment is applied but critical contextual data such as asset classification or account type is missing.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are time-synchronised to the authoritative time source.

part.name: item
part.p: Logs are normalised into the common log schema and enriched with contextual metadata.

part.name: item
part.p: Enriched logs support correlation across relevant systems, environments and data sources in the central logging platform.

part.name: statement
part.p: Ensure detection logic identifies unauthorised changes, anomalous authentication activity and suspicious software execution.

part.name: item
part.p: No detection logic is deployed to identify unauthorised changes, anomalous authentication activity or suspicious software execution events originating from assets.

part.name: item
part.p: Detection relies entirely on manual log review with no automated rules or alerting.

part.name: item
part.p: Detection logic exists but does not cover all three categories (unauthorised changes, anomalous authentication, suspicious execution).

part.name: item
part.p: Rules are deployed but are not tested or tuned on a regular cycle defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Detection logic is deployed, and unauthorised configuration changes, anomalous authentication patterns and suspicious process execution events are captured and produce alerts.

part.name: item
part.p: Detection logic is tested and tuned on a regular cycle defined by the organisation to maintain effectiveness.

part.name: item
part.p: Detection coverage is reviewed following cyber security incidents or significant environmental changes.

part.name: overview
part.p: Cyber security events are analysed in a timely manner to identify cyber security incidents.

part.name: statement
part.p: Triage alerts and events in a timely manner to determine whether cyber security incident thresholds have been met.

part.name: item
part.p: No documented triage process exists.

part.name: item
part.p: Alerts are routinely ignored or left unreviewed.

part.name: item
part.p: No incident severity thresholds are defined.

part.name: item
part.p: A triage process exists but response times are not defined or consistently met.

part.name: item
part.p: Severity thresholds are defined but escalation procedures are informal.

part.name: item
part.p: A documented triage process with defined severity thresholds and response timeframes is in place.

part.name: item
part.p: Alerts are triaged within the timeframes defined by the organisation and escalated where cyber security incident thresholds are met.

part.name: item
part.p: Triage performance is tracked and reported.

part.name: statement
part.p: Use indicators from across identities, applications, data and infrastructure activity rather than isolated signals when identifying cyber security incidents.

part.name: item
part.p: Investigation relies on single-source alerts with no cross-source correlation.

part.name: item
part.p: Correlation rules do not consider signals from multiple data sources.

part.name: item
part.p: Some correlation exists but is limited to specific data source pairs.

part.name: item
part.p: Cross-source investigation is performed manually but not supported by automated correlation.

part.name: item
part.p: Correlation rules and investigation procedures consider signals across identities, applications, data and infrastructure.

part.name: item
part.p: Automated correlation supports detection of multi-stage adversary activity.

part.name: overview
part.p: Cyber security event detection capabilities are regularly evaluated for effectiveness and continuously refined, including by using current strategic and sector-specific cyber threat intelligence, to improve the detection of cyber security events.

part.name: statement
part.p: Review detection coverage periodically to identify gaps arising from new assets, services or architectural changes.

part.name: item
part.p: No review of detection coverage has been conducted within the period defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: No process exists to assess new assets and services for log coverage or detection applicability.

part.name: item
part.p: A review of detection coverage has been conducted but does not cover all recently deployed assets or services.

part.name: item
part.p: Detection gaps have been identified and remediation is planned, but remediation has not been executed within timeframes defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: A detection coverage review has been completed within the cycle defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: New assets and services are assessed for log coverage and detection rule applicability.

part.name: item
part.p: Identified detection gaps are remediated within risk-based timeframes defined by the organisation.

part.name: overview
part.p: Cyber security incident roles and responsibilities are defined, documented and exercised to support the internal and external coordination and management of cyber security incidents, including responsibilities for declaring cyber security incidents and undertaking pre-approved response and recovery activities.

part.name: statement
part.p: Integrate external coordination obligations into cyber security incident response activities where required.

part.name: item
part.p: External coordination requirements for Cyber security incident response activities are neither identified nor documented.

part.name: item
part.p: No defined triggers, contacts or timeframes exist for external reporting.

part.name: item
part.p: External coordination requirements are documented but are not integrated into operational response procedures.

part.name: item
part.p: Contacts and triggers are defined for some but not all required external parties.

part.name: item
part.p: Cyber security incident response procedures include documented external coordination requirements with defined triggers, contacts and timeframes.

part.name: item
part.p: Requirements cover all relevant external parties identified by applicable legal, regulatory, contractual and organisational obligations.

part.name: item
part.p: Coordination procedures have been exercised or invoked and lessons learnt have been incorporated.

part.name: overview
part.p: Cyber security incidents are contained, eradicated and recovered from in a timely manner.

part.name: statement
part.p: Use documented, tested and approved cyber security incident response procedures when responding to cyber security incidents.

part.name: item
part.p: No documented cyber security incident response plan or procedures exist.

part.name: item
part.p: Incident response activities are conducted on an ad hoc basis without any defined roles, escalation paths, procedures or response objectives.

part.name: item
part.p: Available incident records demonstrate systemic failures to contain, eradicate or recover from cyber security incidents within organisationally defined timeframes, and the causes of these failures are not addressed.

part.name: item
part.p: A cyber security incident response plan exists but has not been exercised or invoked within the organisationally defined test cycle.

part.name: item
part.p: The cyber security incident response plan defines roles, escalation paths, and response procedures, but target timeframes or intended response outcomes are not clearly defined.

part.name: item
part.p: Incident records or exercise results demonstrate that response activities do not consistently meet organisationally defined timeframes or intended outcomes, but identified deficiencies are documented and subject to improvement actions.

part.name: item
part.p: An approved cyber security incident response plan is in place and defines roles, escalation paths, response procedures, target timeframes and intended containment, eradication and recovery outcomes.

part.name: item
part.p: The incident response plan and associated procedures have been exercised or invoked within the organisationally defined test cycle.

part.name: item
part.p: Incident records demonstrate that cyber security incidents are contained, eradicated and recovered from within organisationally defined target timeframes and achieve the intended response outcomes, taking into account incident severity, complexity and business impact.

part.name: item
part.p: Where target timeframes or intended outcomes are not achieved, the causes are analysed, improvement actions are assigned and tracked, and relevant plans, procedures and controls are updated.

part.name: item
part.p: Where no relevant cyber security incident has occurred during the assessment period, appropriately scoped exercises demonstrate the organisation’s capability to achieve its target timeframes and intended response outcomes.

part.name: overview
part.p: Lessons learnt from cyber security incidents are captured, and areas for improvement are identified, prioritised and actioned in a timely manner.

part.name: statement
part.p: Perform post-cyber security incident reviews to identify the security gaps that enabled each stage of the cyber security incident.

part.name: item
part.p: Post-incident reviews are not conducted.

part.name: item
part.p: Post-incident reviews are conducted for some incidents but not all that meet the severity threshold defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Reviews are conducted but findings are not documented or actioned.

part.name: item
part.p: Post-incident reviews are conducted for all incidents meeting the severity threshold defined by the organisation.

part.name: item
part.p: Findings identify the specific gaps that enabled each stage of the incident.

part.name: item
part.p: Remediation actions arising from findings are implemented and tracked to closure.

part.name: statement
part.p: Evaluate the monitoring coverage and cyber security incident response procedures following cyber security incidents.

part.name: item
part.p: Detection rules, monitoring coverage and response procedures are not reviewed following incidents.

part.name: item
part.p: Reviews are conducted but do not result in documented changes to detection or response capabilities.

part.name: item
part.p: Some improvements are made but not systematically tracked or validated.

part.name: item
part.p: Detection rules, monitoring coverage and cyber security incident response procedures are reviewed following incidents, with identified lessons incorporated into updates.

part.name: item
part.p: Changes are documented, tested and validated for effectiveness.
